content: 1. Muscle twitching, jerking, spasms, tremors, or other involuntary movements may occur. 2. Stiffening of the arms and legs can happen. 3. You may experience feelings of anxiety, nervousness, confusion, or a sense of dread. 4. Dizziness or lightheadedness may occur. 5. There is a risk of falling or losing consciousness. Kidney Damage 1. Kidney damage is a potential side effect of using nafcillin. 2. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience symptoms such as: A reduced need to urinate. Swelling in the feet, ankles, or legs. Unusual weakness or fatigue. Difficulty breathing or chest pain/pressure. Confusion. Nausea. Seizures. Liver Damage (Hepatotoxicity) 1. Liver damage can occur with nafcillin use. 2. Notify your healthcare provider immediately if you experience: Nausea or vomiting. Stomach or abdominal pain. Fever. Weakness or unusual tiredness. Itching. Loss of appetite. Light-colored stools. Dark-colored urine. Yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes (jaundice). Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea 1. An overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can occur with antibiotics, including nafcillin. 2. This condition, known as antibiotic-associated diarrhea, may develop even up to two months after stopping the medication. 3. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience: Watery diarrhea. Persistent diarrhea. Blood in your stool. Severe stomach cramps. Fever that begins after starting or finishing the medication. Blood Disorders 1. Nafcillin can cause blood disorders such as agranulocytosis, neutropenia, and bone marrow suppression. 2. Stop using nafcillin and seek medical attention immediately if you experience: Fever. Shortness of breath. Pale or yellowish skin. Easy bruising or bleeding. Frequent infections. Unusual weakness or fatigue. Dizziness, lightheadedness, or a feeling of faintness. Headache. Rapid or irregular heartbeat. Precautions: Who Should Not Use Nafcillin? 1. Do not use nafcillin if you are allergic to: Nafcillin itself. Any ingredients in the specific product dispensed. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients in the nafcillin product. Important Information Before Using Nafcillin 1. Nafcillin is typically administered by a healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. 2. If storing nafcillin at home, do not share it with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. 3. Keep nafcillin out of reach of children. Inform Your Healthcare Provider 1. Before using nafcillin, inform your healthcare provider about: All your health conditions. Any prescription or over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are taking. This information helps determine if nafcillin is appropriate for you. Specific Conditions to Discuss 1. Inform your provider if you have: A penicillin allergy or allergies to other medications, corn, or corn products. Asthma. Liver disease. Kidney disease. A history of antibiotic-associated diarrhea. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding 1. It is unknown if nafcillin affects pregnancy or harms an unborn baby. 2. Inform your provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. 3. Nafcillin passes into breast milk, so notify your provider if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed. Drug Interactions 1. There are no known interactions between nafcillin and foods or drinks. 2. It is unclear if alcohol affects nafcillin, but heavy drinking can weaken your immune response and hinder infection recovery. 3. Always inform your provider about any medications or supplements you are taking, especially: Tetracyclines (e.g., doxycycline, minocycline). Warfarin (a blood thinner). Cyclosporine (an immune suppressant). Probenecid (commonly used for gout). Overdose 1. If you or someone else uses too much nafcillin, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. 2. Nafcillin will need to be discontinued, and a healthcare provider may treat your symptoms and provide supportive care. Missed Dose 1. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. 2. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. 3. Do not take double or extra doses. 4. Complete the full prescribed course of nafcillin, even if symptoms improve, to reduce the risk of future infections becoming resistant to nafcillin or similar medications.
